incidents.name: Prisma Finance
incidents.notes: MigrateTroveZap: onFlashLoan did not validate initiator/params, letting anyone migrate (and re-open with attacker params) other users' troves.

sources.ref: onchain review (no exploit tx in this row; DeFiHackLabs src/test/2024-03/Prisma_exp.sol names the vulnerable contract and the attack tx 0x00c503b595946bccaea3d58025b5f9b3726177bbdc9674e634244135282116c7. Incident block located by binary-searching eth_getBlockByNumber to measurement.incidentTimestamp -> ethereum block 19532470, 2024-03-28T12:00:00Z). VICTIM CORRECTED: this row previously pointed at 0xB8FA880840A64c25318989B907cCb58FD7A324Df, which is not the MigrateTroveZap described in the notes but a Prisma ConvexDepositToken - an EIP-1167 clone whose 45-byte runtime hardcodes the ConvexDepositToken master 0x838a35e3a63df3cd27d321f87980f17f51218fa1 (both verified under that name). The MigrateTroveZap is 0xcC7218100da61441905e0c327749972e3cBeE9EE (Etherscan-verified as `MigrateTroveZap`), created 2024-03-20T08:30:35Z at block 19474738 by tx 0xc8d4059c4394812b142dc88a8a8534687bb8857c10f2093bffc9c44a90ee6f56 from 0xd8531a94100f15af7521a7b6e724ac4959e0a025 (a Prisma deployer, also the deployer of the ConvexDepositToken master; not the attacker). The zap is immutable: zero DELEGATECALL opcodes in its runtime, no EIP-1967 Upgraded event, and byte-identical eth_getCode at the creation block and the incident block, so the deployment basis is exact. Code age falls from 122.0 days (measured against the wrong contract) to 703765s, ~8.1 days - the unvalidated onFlashLoan shipped eight days before it was exploited.
merged with the duplicate prisma record, adopting its exploit tx and exact block-timestamp measurement
